Senses.Explanation: Literally, entrust to movement or let the course proceed. The compound occurs 1,101 times in 250 allowlisted texts. As a predicate it describes conduct or functioning that proceeds without forced direction. A Keqin letter gives an explicit comparison: 'what is called proceeding of itself is like a dull-witted person whose household has a capable person caring for him.' Other records pair it with following circumstances in both word orders, with freedom, and with the doubled expansion 'buoyantly proceeding of itself.' Concrete lines place it after drinking when thirsty and eating when hungry, or say that at all times and places one proceeds of oneself freely and responds without a fixed direction.
Senses.Note: The doubled expansion 'buoyantly proceeding of itself' occurs 140 times in 94 texts. 'Proceed of itself and follow circumstances' and its reverse each occur 27 times; 'proceed of itself freely' occurs five times in five texts. This predicate is distinct from the exact title of the seventh oxherding section recorded below.

Senses.Explanation: As an exact title in Puming's oxherding sequence, (任運) names the seventh section. Its verse places the herdboy by the spring river and says that hunger is met by food and thirst by drink as time passes. The title is a named textual unit, not merely another translation of the predicate 'proceed of itself.'
Senses.Note: Two independently allowlisted J23 records preserve the exact seventh-section heading. Their wording is closely related, but each anchors the title as a title.
